records.text: Anonymous correspondents currently stationed at Fort Huachuca told Owens that Joint Task Force–Southern Border was using a borrowed, effectively unmarked building converted into a SCIF with barbed wire and restrictions on personal electronics
records.speaker: Fort Huachuca stationed correspondents (identities unverified)

appearances.snippet: Well, guess what? We have confirmed from people currently stationed on the base. ... that JTF is indeed using a building and not going to name the building I know the exact one, because I don't want to accidentally violate national security, but effectively they are borrowing a building so it's effectively unmarked in that sense, and that that building has been turned into ... Please forgive me if I get this wrong, but I'm reading it direct from the email, SCIF, which stands for a Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility, okay? ... So they have since added barbed wire around that facility for additional security. Cell phones and other electronics are not allowed.

verification.notes: Verification attempted. USNORTHCOM confirms JTF–Southern Border headquarters infrastructure at Fort Huachuca, but no authoritative public source located confirms the alleged borrowed/unmarked building, SCIF conversion, barbed wire, or device rules. The episode attributes those details to unnamed correspondents, so the specific allegation remains unverifiable.

sources.title: New joint task force established to lead USNORTHCOM efforts on southern border
sources.relevance: Officially confirms JTF–Southern Border was activated at Fort Huachuca and that the 10th Mountain Division established its headquarters infrastructure; it does not confirm the alleged building or SCIF details.

conveyance.original_source: Emails from people stationed at Fort Huachuca
